title: "4.7 Limitations and compensating controls"
order: 7
---

The chapter raises five open findings about its own model. Each has evidence drawn from
the facts, a compensating control and an owner. The same five, in the same words, are the
open findings of the validation sign-off (D11, in the validation PDF).

| # | Finding | Evidence | Compensating control | Owner | Status |
|--|--------------|----------------|------------------|-------|------|
| 1 | No out-of-time sample: origination is a single cross-section, so temporal stability is untested. | Train and test are random splits of one cohort; PSI between them ({{< var score.psi_score >}} on the score) measures sampling noise, not drift. | Monitoring plan (D4.8): score and feature PSI on each new cohort, with redevelopment triggers. | Model developer | open |
| 2 | The gate population is not the lending population. | Held-out AUC {{< var score.pop.everyone.auc >}} on all applicants (the gate, {{< var score.gate >}}); {{< var score.pop.booked.auc >}} on the booked only. | Report both on every run; track the booked-only AUC beside the gate; consider gating on the booked population at redevelopment. | Model developer | open |
| 3 | Features with no causal role in the generator are in the model (`industry`, `entity_type`, `trade_lines`). | Together they carry {{< var score.var_share_structural >}} of the logit's variance on the held-out applicants. | Present but inert: remove at the next redevelopment; removal is a simplification, not a risk fix. | Model developer | open |
| 4 | The score distribution is concentrated in one band. | {{< var score.band.D.n >}} of {{< var score.n_test >}} held-out applicants ({{< var score.band_d_share >}}) fall in band D, limiting discrimination inside it. | Downstream decisions use the PD, not the band alone; review band boundaries at redevelopment. | Model developer | open |
| 5 | The weight of evidence of `leverage` is not monotonic, although the generator's effect of leverage is. | Read in bin order, WoE is not monotonic in {{< var score.woe_nonmonotonic >}}; `monotonic_trend` is left at optbinning's `"auto"` default. | Set `monotonic_trend` explicitly for each numeric feature at the next redevelopment and re-verify the gate; until then, discrimination is unaffected, since every performance figure is measured with these bins. | Model developer | open |

## Finding 1 — No out-of-time sample

**Finding.** Every applicant comes from one generated cross-section. Train and test are a
random partition of it ([4.2](data.qmd#split-and-seed)), so nothing in this chapter tests
whether the model holds on a later cohort.

**Evidence.** The score PSI between the splits is {{< var score.psi_score >}} and no
feature exceeds the {{< var monitoring.psi_watch >}} watch level
([4.5](performance.qmd#stability)). That is what a random split of one sample should
show: it measures sampling noise, not drift.

**Impact.** A shift in the applicant population would move the bins' default rates and
the PD in every band. Nothing at development would have warned of it.

**Compensating control.** The monitoring plan ([4.8](monitoring.qmd)): score and feature
PSI, and observed-to-predicted default rates by band, on each new cohort, with thresholds
that trigger review and redevelopment. **Owner:** model developer.

## Finding 2 — The gate population is not the lending population

**Finding.** The model trains and is gated on all applicants. The bank lends only to the
ones it books, and on them the model ranks noticeably worse.

**Evidence.** On the held-out split
([4.2](data.qmd#two-populations)):

- all applicants, the gate's population: AUC {{< var score.pop.everyone.auc >}}
  ({{< var score.pop.everyone.n >}} rows), against the {{< var score.gate >}} gate;
- booked only: AUC {{< var score.pop.booked.auc >}} ({{< var score.pop.booked.n >}} rows);
- rejected only: AUC {{< var score.pop.rejected.auc >}} ({{< var score.pop.rejected.n >}}
  rows).

Much of the whole-population AUC comes from separating the obvious rejections from the
obvious approvals. Among the booked, whom the bank already judged acceptable, the
remaining differences are smaller and harder to rank. This is not a defect of the model:
the generator gives every applicant an outcome. It is a property of where the gate is
measured.

**Impact.** The gate overstates how well the score ranks where lending happens. Pricing,
early warning and line increase all operate on the booked book (D3), in the weaker
population.

**Compensating control.** Report both AUCs on every run; track the booked-only AUC beside
the gate in monitoring ([4.8](monitoring.qmd)); consider gating on the booked population at
redevelopment. The gate itself is not changed by this finding ([4.9](gate.qmd)).
**Owner:** model developer.

## Finding 3 — Features with no causal role are in the model

**Finding.** `industry`, `entity_type` and `trade_lines` are structural zeros: the data
generator gives them no role in default. All three are among the
{{< var score.n_features >}} `FEATURE_COLUMNS`.

**Evidence.** Their fitted contribution was measured before this finding was written:
`feature_contributions` on the held-out applicants, share of the variance of the model's
logit. **They are present but inert: together they carry
{{< var score.var_share_structural >}} of the logit's variance.** Each has an IV below the
{{< var monitoring.iv_useless >}} line ([4.3](methodology.qmd#feature-selection-and-signal)),
and a refit on structural zeros alone ranks at {{< var score.stress.structural_five.auc >}}
([4.6](sensitivity.qmd#structural-zeros-nothing-to-rank-on)).

**Impact.** Small. The three features move the score very little, so removing them is a
simplification, not a risk fix. They do cost something: each adds a WoE table to validate
and monitor, and can surface as a reason code that has no causal basis.

**Compensating control.** Remove them at the next redevelopment, then re-verify the gate.
**Owner:** model developer.

## Finding 4 — The score distribution is concentrated in one band

**Finding.** About half the held-out applicants fall in the riskiest band.

**Evidence.** {{< var score.band.D.n >}} of {{< var score.n_test >}} held-out applicants
({{< var score.band_d_share >}}) are in band D ([4.5](performance.qmd#rank-ordering-and-calibration-by-band)),
where the observed default rate is {{< var score.band.D.observed >}}.

**Impact.** The band cannot distinguish between the applicants inside band D. Any use of the band alone — a rate card, a cutoff, a report — treats them
as one.

**Compensating control.** Downstream decisions use the PD, not the band alone: adjudication,
pricing, early warning and line increase all take the continuous PD or score
([4.1](purpose.qmd#who-consumes-it-and-how)), and pricing by band is a prohibited use.
Review the band boundaries at redevelopment. **Owner:** model developer.

## Finding 5 — The weight of evidence of `leverage` is not monotonic

**Finding.** In the generator, more leverage always means more risk: it enters the default
logit with one sign (`shared/data_generator.py`). In the committed scorecard it does not:
`leverage`'s WoE rises and falls across its bins.

**Evidence.** Read in bin order from the committed card's binning tables, the WoE of
{{< var score.n_woe_nonmonotonic >}} of the {{< var score.n_numeric >}} numeric features is
not monotonic: {{< var score.woe_nonmonotonic >}} ([4.4](assumptions.qmd#monotonic-weight-of-evidence)).
`train.py` calls `BinningProcess` without a `monotonic_trend`, so optbinning's default,
`"auto"`, chose the shape. The break in `leverage` is most likely sampling noise the binning kept: the
generator's effect of leverage is one-signed.
(`trade_lines` has no role in the generator at all, so its shape is noise too; it is
covered by finding 3.)

**Impact.** Not discrimination: every figure in [4.5](performance.qmd) is measured with
these bins. The impact is defensibility: within the range where the WoE turns, an applicant
with more leverage can score better than one with less, and a leverage reason code there
cannot be explained to the applicant.

**Compensating control.** Set `monotonic_trend` explicitly for each numeric feature at the
next redevelopment, then re-verify the gate ([4.9](gate.qmd)). **Owner:** model developer.

## Observations {#observations}

Two matters are recorded but not raised as findings. Each is minor on this data or
already covered by a control above, and each is re-examined at redevelopment.

| Observation | Evidence | Why not a finding | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Some bands are outside the calibration tolerance: A and AAA on all held-out applicants (ratios {{< var score.band.A.ratio >}}, {{< var score.band.AAA.ratio >}}); B, A and AAA on the held-out booked (ratios {{< var score.band_booked.B.ratio >}}, {{< var score.band_booked.A.ratio >}}, {{< var score.band_booked.AAA.ratio >}}) | Few defaults behind each: {{< var score.band.A.defaults >}} and {{< var score.band.AAA.defaults >}} on all applicants; {{< var score.band_booked.B.defaults >}}, {{< var score.band_booked.A.defaults >}} and {{< var score.band_booked.AAA.defaults >}} on the booked ([4.5](performance.qmd#rank-ordering-and-calibration-by-band)) | Too few defaults to distinguish a miscalibration from noise | Watched by the band calibration check on the booked, from these baselines ([4.8](monitoring.qmd#development-baselines)) |
| A missing numeric input is scored as zero | `compute_features` fills missing and non-numeric values with zero ([4.2](data.qmd#features)) | The generated data have no missing values | Reject or refer incomplete applications in any production use ([4.6](sensitivity.qmd#bureau-feed-down-a-gate-failure-documented)) |
